problem: End-to-end trained visual navigation agents (Habitat, AI-Thor) use teleporting or discrete stop-and-go motion in simulation, ignoring robot dynamics, which causes a large sim2real gap in actuation and makes real navigation slow and unreliable. Real-robot evaluations are rare and limited.
motivation: Efficient real navigation needs the robot to keep moving while the network computes, so the agent must anticipate its future state under a realistic motion model. Sensing noise (odometry drift, localization errors) must also be modelled to transfer PointGoal policies trained in photorealistic simulation to real robots.
key_idea: Identify a 2nd-order asymmetric dynamical model of the real robot plus its low-level controller, add it to Habitat as a fast 30Hz inner physics loop, and train an RL agent that predicts discretized velocity commands at 3Hz with noisy odometry and localization models.
insight: Training with the identified motion model is decisive: the same 28-action velocity agent without dynamics gets 0.8% SR in sim+dyn and 20% in real, versus 97.4% and 40% with it (Table 1). The dynamics add little difficulty in simulation (Table 2, similar SR/SPL in the train domain), so the agent learns to anticipate motion. The static goal g0 with proprioceptive/localization inputs beats a dynamic goal from noisy external localization, and removing the localization supervision is surprisingly competitive in real, suggesting insufficient noise modelling.
method: Velocity action space: 28 discrete actions (linear {0,0.3,0.6,1} m/s x angular {-3..3} rad/s), issued asynchronously at 3Hz while the robot keeps moving.

Dynamical model in Habitat: asymmetric 2nd-order model (8 parameters, separate accel/decel for linear and angular) run at 30Hz between 3Hz agent steps, with velocity/acceleration clipping; parameters fit by least squares from 8 real robot trajectories, then damping manually set to 0.7.

Recurrent policy: ResNet-18 RGB + 1D-CNN scan + MLPs for odometry, AMCL pose, static goal g0, and previous-action embedding feed a 2-layer GRU (1024) with actor/critic heads (25.6M params); an auxiliary head predicts the dynamic goal compass supervised by GT pose in sim.
Noise models: integrated odometry with drifting Gaussian noise; absolute localization (AMCL) modelled as non-drifting Gaussian noise delivered irregularly every U(8,12) steps.
Simulated Lidar scan: fused from 4 RealSense depth cameras (points 5cm-1.2m height, 180 azimuth bins, min range), optionally fusing several past frames.

RL training: PPO on 800 HM3D scenes for 200M steps, reward 2.5*success - geodesic gain - 0.01 slack - 0.1 per collision; rudimentary recovery behavior (reverse 2s after 5s stuck) and recurrent state reset every 10s in real.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + 1D-CNN + MLPs + 2-layer GRU policy (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: 800 HM3D scenes in Habitat, 200M env steps of RL; real robot trajectories (8) only for dynamics system identification; optional finetuning on a Matterport scan of the target office
setting.observation: front RGB (256x144) + simulated 180-ray scan from 4 depth cameras + wheel odometry + low-frequency AMCL pose (Lidar-based) + static point goal
setting.action_space: 28 discretized velocity commands (4 linear x 7 angular), executed by closed-loop control at 3Hz
setting.simulator: Habitat (modified with identified dynamical model), HM3D; real Naver Rookie robot
setting.privileged: none at test time beyond a pre-built 2D map for AMCL localization and initial goal vector; GT pose used only for auxiliary supervision in training

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks (HM3D validation episodes, self-collected office episodes) rather than standard named benchmarks; sim Office/20 also reported in Table 1 (SR 100.0, SPL 78.8, SCT 59.9).
results: With the identified motion model, the agent reaches 97.4% SR / 82.2% SPL in simulation with dynamics and 40% SR in real, vs 58.2% sim / 15% real for a position-command agent and 0.8% sim / 20% real for velocity commands without dynamics. Finetuned on the target building it reaches 55-60% real SR, still below the map-based ROS 2 planner (80-90% SR) which has many more collisions.
limitations: Real-world success remains modest (40-60% on only 20 episodes) and below the ROS 2 map-based planner in SR/SPL/SCT.
Agent gets discouraged by blockings, requiring a hack of resetting the recurrent state every 10s; sensor/odometry noise modelling is insufficient.
Dynamics manually tuned (damping) and evaluated on a single robot and office environment with a tiny real test set.
